findings: Resolved the registered local PDF and checked its 36-page identity against the previous audit hash. The source is arXiv:2210.14429v2, stamped 30 August 2023 with cover date 1 September 2023; journal-version equivalence is not asserted.

Enumerated the actual main-text theorem headings on pages 1-17 and the part of page 18 above y=421: Theorem 1 on page 12, Theorem 4 on pages 15-16, and Theorem 5 on page 17. Results 2 and 3 are Corollaries. The Appendix A heading starts at y=422.38 on page 18; its body and pages 19-36 were excluded.

Compared the full original statements with rendered source pages 12, 15, 16 and 17. Theorem 1 retains both the depth-K and penalized-pruning oracle inequalities, including the second infimum over K. It requires Assumption 2, not Assumption 1 or exact membership of mu in F.

Theorem 4 retains d=p, kappa=1, unit split-success probability and Assumptions 2-4, both rates, the constant declaration, the penalty lower bound and the page-16 continuation. No additional moment assumption from the preceding proof lemma was imported.

Theorem 5 preserves its printed grammar and the subsample size N in all complexity factors, distinct from n in the tree bounds. Its following paragraph changes the inverse-probability expectation to subsampled data. No pruned or fast-rate forest theorem was inferred from discussion.

Checked all 13 original source entries against pages 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 14, 15 and 16. The observation model, globally normalized split criterion, candidate-success event, stopping rule and node-average prediction retain their original scopes. Purely random directions are examples rather than a unique required law.

Kept finite ridge variation, finite ridge library and the L2(P_x) closure with relaxed local variation distinct. The source leaves notation binding, endpoint values and representative conventions unresolved; existing notes preserve those issues separately from quotations.

Pruning retains the original empirical-loss-plus-leaf-penalty objective. The source descriptions of the smallest subtree and decreasing unpenalized error are not silently repaired. Assumption 2 retains its uniform conditional exponential-tail quantifiers and positive constants.

Assumption 3 retains its common q>2 and uniform-depth aggregate local-variation bound. Assumption 4 retains the same q, the threshold on nu and its literal all-K node-count moment bound. The existing note about incompatibility with finite-sample stopping remains separate from the original statement.

The forest uses size-N sampling without replacement and B randomizations sharing the original data. Conditional independence and the unspecified subsampling law are distinguished in analysis. The forest output depends on tree means indirectly for Theorem 5.

Rechecked the 12 ambient passages, including population versus empirical norms, internal nodes [T] versus terminal nodes T, joint data/search-space expectations, inverse-probability integrability, the formal empty internal node, and the main-text announcement of generalized node fits. Appendix references remain unresolved within the main-text-only scope.

Reviewed the 21 direct theorem edges and the recursive local graph against the statements and source passages. All three theorems reach D1-D8 and D10. Only Theorems 1 and 4 reach pruning D9, only Theorem 4 reaches Assumptions 3/4 (D11/D12), and only Theorem 5 reaches forest construction D13. The resulting deduplicated total is 32 related-theorem connections.

Reviewed every source-derived natural-language name, the three assumption-heading naming contexts and all highlight selectors. Distinctive notation or actual source labels identify the intended objects. No synthesized definition or generic relationship caption was added.

The six existing census-content JSON artifacts required no changes. Archived the previous scripts and made the retained per-paper extraction scripts runnable in an empty output directory with verified local source resolution. Regeneration reproduced all six artifacts byte for byte and did not rewrite source-review records.

Independent inventory and census validators check structure, inventory identity and graph consistency; they do not replace the manual PDF comparison described above. Source ambiguities remain recorded in ambient-conventions.json rather than corrected inside original quotations.
